- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment strength.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >80) — cap forecast at +3% above true peak or adjust downward by 1–2% per subsequent day.
- Lagged forecast errors: if true price rises >5% from prior day, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next day.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate volatility — reduce final 5–7 days by 1–2% to align with observed tapering.
